root_cause: Steam coil E-101 fouled progressively (deposit build-up), reducing coil heat-transfer capability so TV-101 had to open further for the same steam flow and duty
notes: TV-101 drifted up to ~4.5 % above the position the clean-coil model needs, with a decelerating ramp, then stepped back to normal at ~05:50 on 03-22. Ruled out: steam meter error (energy balance steam vs process stays ~0), header pressure/Tsat loss (PI-201 and TI-201 normal), positioner fault (TV-101.POS tracks FIC-201.OP), steam trap/condensate backup (TI-201 - TI-202 subcooling stays ~4.8 K), agitator/mixing (TI-102 tracks TIC-101.PV). Alternative not fully excluded: restriction in TV-101 trim.

root_cause: Steam trap on the E-101 condensate outlet partially blocked (failing to discharge), so condensate backed up and flooded part of the coil
notes: Condensate subcooling (TI-201 - TI-202, TI-202 shifted 4 min) rose from ~5 K to ~12.5 K together with TV-101 opening ~5.5 % above model for the same steam flow: waterlogged coil loses active area. Subcooling cycles over ~1.5 h, as with a trap intermittently passing. Both recover together at ~00:15-01:00 on 04-08. Header pressure, steam meter (energy balance) and positioner all normal.

root_cause: Product flow transmitter FI-102 developed a step zero offset, reading about 0.4 m3/h low
notes: Abrupt step in FI-101 - FI-102 of +0.40 m3/h and in FI-102 vs the valve equation (21.24 x LV-101.POS x sqrt(level)) of -0.4 m3/h. Level constant on both transmitters and LV-101 position unchanged, so the true outflow equals feed. Offset independent of flow (slope 0.005) and FI-102 noise unchanged. Energy balance normal so FI-101 is correct. Alternative not excluded: leak between LV-101 and FI-102.

root_cause: Steam control valve TV-101 sticking (stiction from high stem/packing friction): stem holds position while demand changes, then jumps (stick-slip)
notes: TV-101.POS stays flat for ~20+ min while FIC-201.OP moves by >1 %, then jumps. Position-demand deviation (10-min median) rises from a normal <=0.3 % to 0.5-1.4 % from 04-26, worst 04-27 to 04-30, normal again from ~22:00 on 05-01. Steam flow cycles around setpoint in step with the jumps. Onset is gradual, so the start is approximate.

root_cause: Primary level transmitter LI-101 (LIC-101.PV) drifted high at an abnormal rate (~4.5 cm in ~40 h, far above normal calibration drift), so LIC-101 drove the real level down
notes: LIC-101.PV held at 2.00 m while the redundant LI-102 fell to 1.955 m. The level inferred from the valve equation using FI-102 and LV-101.POS also fell (1.945 to 1.90 m), and LV-101 opened ~0.7 % for unchanged flow, so the real level dropped: LI-102 is right and LI-101 is wrong. Rate ~0.7 % of span per day vs ~0.012 %/day typical drift. Snapped back at ~21:30 on 05-05.

root_cause: Liquid leak from TK-101 (vessel or outlet piping upstream of LV-101), growing to about 2 m3/h of product lost before the outlet valve
notes: FI-101 - FI-102 grew from 0 to 2.0 m3/h over ~3 days, then plateaued. Level constant on both transmitters while LV-101 closed from 50 % to 43.5 %, and FI-102 agrees with the valve equation, so less liquid really passes LV-101. Steam use and the steam-vs-process energy balance are unchanged, so the full metered feed (FI-101 correct) enters and is heated: the missing liquid leaves the tank at bulk temperature by another route. Ended abruptly at ~05:45 on 05-27.
Not claimed as a fault: FIC-201 scan-rate oscillation with a steam flow reading excursion. Same signature as 03-02 09:15-10:45, which is inside the declared-normal baseline. Temperature unaffected.
TIC-101 setpoint 75 to 78 degC and back; normal response.
TIC-101 in MAN; temperature drifted with heat demand as expected (steam-side residuals normal).
LIC-101 setpoint 2.0 to 2.3 m and back; normal response.
TIC-101.PV not stored for 14 h (grid is interpolated); TI-102 and controller output behave normally.
